source: Advanced short story written in spoken Palestinian by Claude. NOT native-validated.

sentences.ar: قبل ما يوصل الكهربا عالضيعة، كان الناس يستعملوا قناديل.
sentences.en: Before electricity reached the village, people used lanterns.

sentences.ar: جدي كان عنده قنديل قديم بيضويله الليل.
sentences.en: My grandfather had an old lantern that lit up his night.

sentences.ar: كل مسا، كان يشعله ويحطه عالطاولة.
sentences.en: Every evening, he would light it and put it on the table.

sentences.ar: حواليه، كانت العيلة تجتمع تحكي وتضحك.
sentences.en: Around it, the family would gather to talk and laugh.

sentences.ar: جدي كان يحكينا قصص عالضو الخافت.
sentences.en: My grandfather would tell us stories by the dim light.

sentences.ar: كنا نسمعه ونحن مشدودين، وظلالنا عالحيط.
sentences.en: We would listen to him, captivated, our shadows on the wall.

sentences.ar: لما إجت الكهربا، الكل فرح بالضو الجديد.
sentences.en: When electricity came, everyone was happy with the new light.

sentences.ar: بس جدي ضل يحب قنديله القديم.
sentences.en: But my grandfather kept loving his old lantern.

sentences.ar: قلتله: يا جدي، الكهربا أحسن وأقوى.
sentences.en: I told him: grandpa, electricity is better and stronger.

sentences.ar: ابتسم وقال: الضو القوي بيوري كل شي.
sentences.en: He smiled and said: strong light shows everything.

sentences.ar: قال: بس ضو القنديل بيخلي القلوب تقرب.
sentences.en: He said: but the lantern's light makes hearts draw closer.
I didn't understand his words when I was young.

sentences.ar: بس هلأ، وكل واحد غارق بتلفونه، فهمت.
sentences.en: But now, with everyone lost in their phone, I understand.
I still keep my grandfather's lantern to this day.

sentences.ar: وكل ما أشعله، بترجع تلك الليالي الدافية.
sentences.en: And every time I light it, those warm nights come back.
